newsitem.title: UK: NatWest reiterates UK job, cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: NatWest reiterates UK job, cost cuts.

text.p: Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc on Wednesday reiterated that it would shed at least 10,000 jobs in its UK retail banking operations over the next five years but said it planned no compulsory redundancies.
In a progress report on its "Building a New Retail Bank" strategy announced in May, NatWest said the move was in response to increased competition and changing customer behaviour.
The strategy will also contribute to the goal of cutting the cost/income ratio in the UK bank to 63 percent by the turn of the century from 67.8 percent currently.
Tim Jones, managing director of retail banking, said the bank had forged positive relationships with the trade unions at NatWest and praised their contribution to managing the transition.

Jones said NatWest was going ahead with plans to drastically reduce its processing capacity with 60 locations handling cheque processing, account management, and cash handling which was previously done in branches and 150 centres around the country.
